The first underwater cable beneath the English Channel was laid in 1850 [d1][d3][d6]. It was laid by John Watkins Brett and his brother Jacob Brett, running from Dover to Calais [d3][d6]. According to d3, it "consisted of a single No.14 copper wire with gutta percha insulation and no armouring" and "worked only briefly" — indeed, a French fisherman reportedly cut it, thinking it was a new kind of seaweed [d6]. An improved, armored cable was subsequently laid in 1851 and became operational to the public on November 13, 1851 [d10].
